title: Comparing Structs
story: You and your friend are arguing about who is older — by only a few months! Instead of doing the math yourself, you'll write a function that compares Person structs.
why: Comparing structs lets you sort, filter, and make decisions based on data — like finding the oldest person or checking if two ages match.
analogy: Comparing structs is like comparing two trading cards — you look at specific stats (fields) to decide which one is better, older, or bigger.
try_it: Add a `youngest_of_three` function that takes three Persons and returns the name of the youngest. Test it with three different ages.
tips: Access struct fields with dot notation even inside comparison functions: `a.age > b.age`
Comparison functions return Bool — name them like questions: `is_older`, `same_age`, `has_longer_name`
You can compare any field type: Int with `>`, Str with `==`, Float64 with `>`
common_mistakes: Comparing Int fields with `==` for "is older" instead of `>` — `==` checks equality, not greater-than
Accessing the wrong person's field — `a.age > a.age` compares a person to themselves (always false)
Forgetting that `is_older(a, b)` returns false when they're the SAME age — `>` is strict, not `>=`
